reason: Reproduced exactly. render-b.js:574 renders undoBar() as a sibling after .b-two and before foot(), i.e. at the tail of the document, and b.css:490 gives it no positioning at all. Driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing and pressing .b-step[data-delta="7"] with no scrolling: .b-undo lands at top 1911 in a 960 viewport (1440 and 1280 alike, editor plate ends at y=914) and at top 2263 in an 844 viewport; inView false in all three. So the one surface that says the change can be taken back sits ~1000-1400px below the button that made it. Not restated by the gates: interaction-check proves the bar is live, singular, silent when empty and keyboard-safe, none of which is placement. Not already handled: the visible aftermath at the point of action is the .b-stepRead date readout, which confirms the change but says nothing about reversing it, and Ctrl Z is only advertised on the off-screen bar itself. The fix is right in intent but wrong in one half and imprecise in the other, so it needs sharpening rather than adopting as written.
sharpenedFix: Keep ONE .b-undo node and never re-parent it on a breakpoint. (1) In render-b.js ownerSurface, move undoBar() out of the field tail and into the rail column: h("div.b-stick", ...[horizon({}), h("div.b-editHost"), undoBar()]). At 1280+ .b-stick is already position:sticky;top:24px (b.css:738) and the rail measures 723px with the editor open, so the bar lands around y=750 in view with NO sticky of its own - drop the proposed 'position:sticky;bottom:24px', which is redundant when the rail fits and, when it does not (short laptop viewports), detaches the bar from the editor plate and floats it at the viewport edge, i.e. the toast the finding says it must not be. (2) Do NOT put it inside the fixed sheet below 1280. .b-edit is created in openEditor and destroyed by closeEditor (node.remove()), so a strip inside it would take the undo message with it the moment the owner presses Done or Escape - today the message correctly survives that (verified), and the fix as written would trade an off-screen safety net for one that is deleted at the exact step back where it is wanted. It would also sit inside a max-height:72dvh overflow-y:auto box and scroll away. Instead promote the same node under a max-width:1279px query: .b-undo { position: fixed; left: 12px; right: 12px; bottom: 12px; z-index: 4; } and, so the two do not stack on each other, set the root flag already implied by paintUndo (e.g. root data-undo="true" when history is non-empty) and lift the sheet with [data-undo="true"] .b-edit { bottom: 76px; } plus matching bottom padding on .b-field so the last rows are never covered. (3) Keep data-empty="true" -> display:none for the resting state as proposed, but note display:none cannot transition: to get the 0.14s appear, animate opacity with @starting-style (or swap display for a zero-height, visibility:hidden rest state) using var(--t-base), which is already 0.14s in shell.css:44 - do not introduce a new duration.
